ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and points A, B, and C are all on the circumference. Line segments AB and AC are chords of the circle, and intersect at point A to form ∠A. On the right side of the circle, near the arc from B to C, 170° is marked, indicating that the measure of arc BC intercepted by ∠A is 170°. Reasoning: ∠A is an inscribed angle, and it intercepts arc BC. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of an inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of the arc it intercepts. Therefore m∠A = 170° ÷ 2 = 85°.

method.method_draft: Use the inscribed angle theorem. From the image, identify a circle with points A, B, and C on the circumference, with chords AB and AC meeting at A. The label 170° is placed by the arc from B to C on the right side of the circle, indicating the measure of intercepted arc BC. From the text, the target is m∠A. Since ∠A is an inscribed angle intercepting arc BC, its measure is half the measure of that arc: m∠A = 170° / 2 = 85°.
